headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: broad egress plus writable marketing skills can expose shared content and overwrite shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing/list agent with broad network egress, and Agent B explicitly uses shared skill files and shared context. If B ingests A’s generated text from a shared workspace or copied output, prompt-like instructions embedded in content could be followed. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Agent B reads content produced by Agent A from a shared file or copied text, injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions, malicious text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of A’s outputs by B.
Add a manual review step before B consumes any A-generated text.
Prefix A outputs with a non-executable delimiter and strip instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write filesystem content and call external APIs, while Agent A has broad network egress. If they share files or context, marketing content or other workspace data can flow from A into B’s outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred and kept at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share any filesystem path, B can read A-produced content.
IF B sends file contents to GitHub or marketing-skills.com, workspace data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Remove secrets and sensitive drafts from shared folders.
Restrict B’s outbound API targets to a test endpoint.
Review B’s file inputs before any upload.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and spawn_subprocesses, plus multiple-instance support; Agent A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent. If both operate on the same directory, B can overwrite or race on shared files while A produces content that B may also modify or publish. The shared-write pathway is plausible from the profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF B runs multiple instances against shared files, conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a unique working directory.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent B instances on shared paths.
Use read-only mounts for A’s inputs.
requires-engineering: add transactional file updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s sandboxing says skills reference each other and build on shared context, so B may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. If A supplies marketing copy or facts that B then reuses without verification, errors can cascade into downstream content. This is an inferred interaction, but the shared-context design makes the pathway credible.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated copy as shared context, mistakes can propagate.
IF B publishes or forwards that content without verification, the error becomes user-visible.
mitigations: Require source checks before reuse.
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts.
Add a second-pass review for factual claims.
Limit B to summarizing rather than asserting A content.
requires-engineering: implement citation/traceability checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches marketing content and product marketing context and has outbound API/file surfaces, while Agent A is a content-writing agent with broad egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined content flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated or customer-identifying marketing data is placed into either agent, compliance review is needed.
IF outbound API calls carry retained content, retention policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent.
Review outbound destinations before use.
Document retention for marketing drafts.
Delete temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls.
